issues.issue_title: USB buffer overflow on clear stall operation
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: USB buffer overflow on clear stall operation
Context: repo=stm32f0xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=USB, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=9
Root cause: Hi @pierre-x, Thank you for this analysis and the proposal you made.
Fix: Inside stm32f0xx_hal_pcd.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, USB, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, needs clarification, pcd, CDC_Receive_FS, USBD_CDC_ReceivePacket, xfer_count, USBD_LL_ClearStallEP

Technical details:
Inside stm32f0xx_hal_pcd.c, on normal operation, when the receive buffer is not full, the receive callback CDC_Receive_FS calls USBD_CDC_ReceivePacket, which re-arms the endpoint to receive new data and sets ep->xfer_count to zero. In the case of a full buffer, the host may reach a timeout and request a Clear Stall. USBD_LL_ClearStallEP will call HAL_PCD_EP_ClrStall to re-arm the endpoint WITHOUT resetting ep->xfer_count, which will cause a buffer overflow when receiving the next packet. IMHO, HAL_PCD_EP_ClrStall() should include an ep->xfer_count = 0. The tricky part: the host can send Clear Stalls at any time, even when the buffer isn't full and the device isn't Stalled, in this case the buffer index shouldn't be cleared. So maybe the solution is something like that: HAL_StatusTypeDef HAL_PCD_EP_ClrStall(PCD_HandleTypeDef *hpcd, uint8_t ep_addr) { // [...] if(ep->is_flowcontrol_triggered) { ep->xfer_count = 0; }

Key comments:
Hi @pierre-x, Thank you for this analysis and the proposal you made. I will forward your report to our development teams for further analysis. I will keep you informed. @pierre-x, May I ask whether the use case you reported has been tested by any means and the described issue reproduced, or is it analysis based on code review? Thank you, ST Internal Reference: 201910 > May I ask whether the use case you reported has been tested by any means and the described issue reproduced, or is it analysis based on code review? It's a bug we have encountered, and that we can reproduce 100% of the time. We have corrected it as described in the bug report. I can share by email some part of our source code if necessary. Hi @pierre-x, May I ask you whether you can share a sample project allowing to reproduce the issue? Thank you, Hi @pierre-x, Any sample code or project to share please? Thank you, Hi @pierre-x, Any sample code or project to share please? Thank you, Hi @pierre-x, Please allow me to close this thread as no reply since a while. Do not hesitate to log another one in case you believe the point is still relevant. Thank you for your comprehension.

Problem: Unused parameter warning in function 'LL_RCC_ConfigMCO'
Context: repo=stm32f0xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=LL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=8
Root cause: ST Internal Reference: 200686 Fixed in 51e49ecc6425d24bddb5ef8d4eaaaff97bf1b7a9
Fix: In function LL_RCC_ConfigMCO, #if defined(RCC_CFGR_MCOPRE) results in unused MCOxPrescaler function parameter when defined and leads to warning: unused parameter 'MCOxPrescaler' [-Wunused-parameter] when gcc build this header.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: LL, bug_report, medium, bug, hal, internal bug tracker, rcc, LL_RCC_ConfigMCO, RCC_CFGR_MCOPRE, MODIFY_REG, CFGR, RCC_CFGR_MCOSEL

Technical details:
In function LL_RCC_ConfigMCO, #if defined(RCC_CFGR_MCOPRE) results in unused MCOxPrescaler function parameter when defined and leads to warning: unused parameter 'MCOxPrescaler' [-Wunused-parameter] when gcc build this header. https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f0xx-hal-driver/blob/583049ace060acf646b0fb007938253f71184160/Inc/stm32f0xx_ll_rcc.h#L1228 I can suggest to add (void)MCOxPrescaler to suppress this warning this way: cpp #else (void)MCOxPrescaler; MODIFY_REG(RCC->CFGR, RCC_CFGR_MCOSEL, MCOxSource); #endif /* RCC_CFGR_MCOPRE */

Key comments:
ST Internal Reference: 200686 Fixed in 51e49ecc6425d24bddb5ef8d4eaaaff97bf1b7a9

issues.issue_title: Missing break-statement in LL_ADC_DeInit() can cause software to get stuck in a wait-loop
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Missing break-statement in LL_ADC_DeInit() can cause software to get stuck in a wait-loop
Context: repo=stm32f0xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=NUCLEO-F031K6, component=ADC, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=7
Root cause: ST Internal Reference: 187367 Fixed in commit https://github.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** * Nucleo-F031K6 * STM32CubeIDE 1.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: NUCLEO-F031K6, HAL, ADC, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, GCC, LL_ADC_DeInit, timeout_cpu_cycles, ADC_TIMEOUT_DISABLE_CPU_CYCLES, LL_ADC_IsDisableOngoing

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** * Nucleo-F031K6 * STM32CubeIDE 1.15.0 with GCC 12.3 Rel 1 **Describe the bug** Function LL_ADC_DeInit() contains a wait loop, with timeout detection to make sure the software doesn't hang in case of an unexpected hardware state: c timeout_cpu_cycles = ADC_TIMEOUT_DISABLE_CPU_CYCLES; while (LL_ADC_IsDisableOngoing(ADCx) == 1U) { if(timeout_cpu_cycles-- == 0U) { /* Time-out error */ status = ERROR; } } The bug is that there is a missing break; statement, in case the timeout occurs. This causes the software to potentially still hang in this loop. **How To Reproduce** You can reproduce the problem: 1. Configure and enable the ADC1 on a channel to perform continuous conversions. 2. Call LL_ADC_DeInit(ADC1); This causes the software to hang, because it is stuck in the before mentioned wait loop. **Additional context** Proposed solution: Add the break; statement: c timeout_cpu_cycles = ADC_TIMEOUT_DISABLE_CPU_CYCLES; while (LL_ADC_IsDisableOngoing(ADCx) == 1U) { if(timeout_cpu_cycles-- == 0U) { /* Time-out error */ status = ERROR; break; /* <<< ADDED */ } }

Key comments:
ST Internal Reference: 187367 Fixed in commit https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f0xx_hal_driver/commit/1c14d36d88722f9cd7ed48d842b5ad07330008c7

issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: FLASH_OB_GetRDP has 32-bit return type but HAL_FLASHEx_OBErase implicitly converts it to 8-bits
Context: repo=stm32f0xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=open, issue_number=6
Root cause: See also [stm32f1xx_hal_driver#7](https://github.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** * Hardware agnostic (encountered while compiling program for STM32F072) * STM32CubeIDE v1.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, flash, STM32F072, UTC, DDEBUG, DUSE_HAL_DRIVER, CMSIS, MMD

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** * Hardware agnostic (encountered while compiling program for STM32F072) * STM32CubeIDE v1.14.0 (build 19471_20231121_1200 (UTC)) **Describe the bug** Compiling [stm32f0xx_hal_flash_ex.c](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f0xx_hal_driver/blob/0c66a5bd9c5a1ba51f40d26f2387b3ee44b495d2/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_flash_ex.c#L105) results in (conversion related) warnings at build-time like this: ... arm-none-eabi-gcc "../Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_rcc_ex.c" -mcpu=cortex-m0 -std=gnu11 -g3 -DDEBUG -DUSE_HAL_DRIVER -DSTM32F072xB -c -I../Core/Inc -I../Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Inc -I../Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/Legacy -I../Drivers/CMSIS/Device/ST/STM32F0xx/Include -I../Drivers/CMSIS/Include -Og -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -Wall -Wconversion -fstack-usage -fcyclomatic-complexity -MMD -MP -MF"Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_rcc_ex.d" -MT"Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_rcc_ex.o" --specs=nano.specs -mfloat-abi=soft -mthumb -o "Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_rcc_ex.o" ../Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_flash_ex.c: In function 'HAL_FLASHEx_OBErase': ../Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_flash_ex.c:317:12: warning: conversion from 'uint32_t' {aka 'long unsigned int'} to 'uint8_t' {aka 'unsigned char'} may change value [-Wconversion] 317 | rdptmp = FLASH_OB_GetRDP(); | ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ../Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_flash_ex.c: In function 'HAL_FLASHEx_OBGetConfig': ../Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_flash_ex.c:449:23: warning: conversion from 'uint32_t' {aka 'long unsigned int'} to 'uint8_t' {aka 'unsigned char'} may change value [-Wconversion] 449 | pOBInit->RDPLevel = FLASH_OB_GetRDP(); | ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ... 13:52:02 Build Finished. 0 errors, 2 warnings. (took 4s.966ms **How To Reproduce** 1. Application agnostic. 2. Suspect is HAL ([stm32f0xx_hal_flash_ex.c](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f0xx_hal_driver/blob/5fd31c52559a593dd9038c4abb4b85faeac728c6/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_flash_ex.c#L105)) 3. No need to make any calls to reproduce -- problem is warning at compile time. 4. Can reproduce by compiling stm32f0xx_hal_flash_ex.c with conversion warnings enabled. **Additional context** My suggested solution is to simply change the return type from uint32_t to uint8_t since result must be one of [OB_RDP_LEVEL_0, OB_RDP_LEVEL_1, or OB_RDP_LEVEL_2](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f0xx_hal_driver/blob/5fd31c52559a593dd9038c4abb4b85faeac728c6/Inc/stm32f0xx_hal_flash_ex.h#L298-L301) patch diff --git a/Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_flash_ex.c b/Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_flash_ex.c index 7ea91b9..34068c7 100644 --- a/Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_flash_ex.c +++ b/Drivers/STM32F0xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_flash_ex.c @@ -102,7 +102,7 @@ static HAL_StatusTypeDef FLASH_OB_RDP_LevelConfig(uint8_t ReadProtectLevel); static HAL_StatusTypeDef FLASH_OB_UserConfig(uint8_t UserConfig); static HAL_StatusTypeDef FLASH_OB_ProgramData(uint32_t Address, uint8_t Data); static uint32_t FLASH_OB_GetWRP(void); -static uint32_t FLASH_OB_GetRDP(void); +static uint8_t FLASH_OB_GetRDP(void); static uint8_t FLASH_OB_GetUser(void); /** @@ -899,7 +899,7 @@ static uint32_t FLASH_OB_GetWRP(void) * @arg @ref OB_RDP_LEVEL_1 Read protection of the memory * @arg @ref OB_RDP_LEVEL_2 Full chip protection */ -static uint32_t FLASH_OB_GetRDP(void) +static uint8_t FLASH_OB_GetRDP(void) { uint32_t tmp_reg;

Key comments:
See also [stm32f1xx_hal_driver#7](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f1xx_hal_driver/pull/7) If changing the signature is too much to ask, perhaps an explicit cast to suppress the warning would be OK? https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f0xx_hal_driver/blob/5fd31c52559a593dd9038c4abb4b85faeac728c6/Src/stm32f0xx_hal_flash_ex.c#L317 c rdptmp = (uint8_t)FLASH_OB_GetRDP(); Then again, these are static ("private implementation details") so I don't see how fixing this would negatively impact any user code. Hello @jacobq, Thank you for your report. We confirm the appearance of warnings by activating -Wconversion warnings. This problem has been reported to our development teams for further analysis. We'll get back to you as soon as we have any updates. ST Internal Reference: CDM0061692

issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: USB HID Keyboard stopped working on STM32Cube FW_F0 V1.11.3
Context: repo=stm32f0xx-hal-driver, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=USB, layer=HAL, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=medium, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=4
Root cause: Hi @DeckerCHAN, Would you mind running one of these two applications from version 1.
Fix: **Caution** The Issues are strictly limited for the reporting of problem encountered with the software provided in this project.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, USB, usage_question, medium, needs clarification, STM32, STM32F042K6U6, FW_F0, USBD_HID_SendReport, HAL_Delay, BSP

Technical details:
**Caution** The Issues are strictly limited for the reporting of problem encountered with the software provided in this project. For any other problem related to the STM32 product, the performance, the hardware characteristics and boards, the tools the environment in general, please post a topic in the [ST Community/STM32 MCUs forum](https://community.st.com/s/group/0F90X000000AXsASAW/stm32-mcus) **Describe the set-up** * Custom board with STM32F042K6U6 * STM32CubeMX + Clion **Describe the bug** A clear and concise description of what the bug is. Custome board simulate keyboard keep pressing CapLock preventing PC from entering sleep. Programming following this post https://controllerstech.com/how-to-use-stm32-as-a-keyboard/ It was working all good by utilising STM32Cude FW_F0 V1.11.2 but stopped working on V1.11.3 The key was pressed but never released. **How To Reproduce** 1. Indicate the global behavior of your application project C keyboardhid[3] = 0x39; USBD_HID_SendReport(&hUsbDeviceFS, (uint8_t *) &keyboardhid, sizeof(keyboardhid)); HAL_Delay(50); keyboardhid[3] = 0x00; USBD_HID_SendReport(&hUsbDeviceFS, (uint8_t *) &keyboardhid, sizeof(keyboardhid)); HAL_Delay(1000); 2. The modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem (Driver, BSP, MW ...) Recent updates on stm32f0xx_hal_pcd.c and stm32f0xx_ll_usb.c 3. The use case that generates the problem https://controllerstech.com/how-to-use-stm32-as-a-keyboard/ 4. How we can reproduce the problem Just follow the post above I will utilise a logic analyser to compare traffic between the two versions. I can provide a video but don't know where I can upload it.

Key comments:
Hi @DeckerCHAN, Would you mind running one of these two applications from version 1.11.3 of the official STM32CubeF0 firmware on your board and check whether you can reproduce the issue you reported? Thank you in advance for your reply. * [STM32F072B-Discovery#HID_Standalone](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF0/tree/master/Projects/STM32F072B-Discovery/Applications/USB_Device/HID_Standalone) * [STM32072B_EVAL#HID_Standalone](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF0/tree/master/Projects/STM32072B_EVAL/Applications/USB_Device/HID_Standalone) There should be no difficulty in porting them as both F072 and F046 have identical USB HAL-LL drivers and use the same USB library. Hi @DeckerCHAN, I hope you are fine. Any feedback please? In the meanwhile, please allow me to close this issue as no activity has been registered since a while. We can easily reopen it should you have any updates to share. Thank you for your comprehension.
